<!-- Author: Kunru Song -->

This report creates the stage-specific item-level data entry for all Step 2
measurement analyses. It extracts raw baseline Trait PSMU, depression, anxiety,
and perceived-stress responses plus raw EMA PSMU manifestation responses from
the prepared `dat_focal_analysis.rda` entry, keeps the participant and prompt
observation levels separate, and saves one RDA containing one stable top-level
object.

No item is reversed or rescaled. No total, mean, factor score, person mean, or
day-level aggregate is stored in the output object. The descriptive summaries at the end of this report check the saved data and are not added to the canonical Step 2 RDA.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  collapse = FALSE,
  comment = NA
)

required_packages <- c(
  "dplyr",
  "ggplot2",
  "knitr",
  "lme4",
  "psych",
  "rmarkdown",
  "svglite",
  "tibble",
  "tidyr"
)
package_available <- vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
if (!all(package_available)) {
  stop(
    "Missing required R packages: ",
    paste(names(package_available)[!package_available], collapse = ", ")
  )
}

locate_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
  current <- normalizePath(start, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
  if (!dir.exists(current)) current <- dirname(current)
  repeat {
    if (all(dir.exists(file.path(current, c(
      "Step_1_Descriptive_and_Reliability", "Step_2_Measurement_Models"
    ))))) return(current)
    parent <- dirname(current)
    if (identical(parent, current)) break
    current <- parent
  }
  stop("Could not locate the project from its public Step directories")
}

input_path <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
project_root <- locate_project_root(if (is.null(input_path)) getwd() else input_path)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dev = "svglite")

input_file <- file.path(
  project_root,
  "Res_2_Data_for_Analysis",
  "dat_focal_analysis.rda"
)
output_file <- file.path(
  project_root,
  "Res_2_Data_for_Analysis",
  "dat_step2_measurement.rda"
)

if (!file.exists(input_file)) {
  stop("Missing prepared input RDA: ", input_file)
}
```

# Variable specification

The extraction is deliberately limited to items used in Step 2. Baseline BSMAS
Items 1--6 and EMA `PMU1`--`PMU2` are mapped to Peripheral; baseline BSMAS
Items 7--18 and EMA `PMU3`--`PMU6` are mapped to Core. The baseline depression,
anxiety, and perceived-stress items are retained for the S2.4 latent SEM. These
are theoretical item-group labels, not factor scores.

```{r variable-specification}
baseline_items <- paste0("V_BSMAS_", 1:18)
depression_items <- paste0("K_CESD_", 1:7)
anxiety_items <- paste0("L_DASS_", 1:7)
stress_items <- paste0("M_PSS_", 1:10)
baseline_outcome_items <- c(depression_items, anxiety_items, stress_items)
baseline_all_items <- c(baseline_items, baseline_outcome_items)
ema_items <- paste0("PMU", 1:6)

baseline_required <- c("Name_ID", baseline_all_items)
ema_required <- c("Data_ID", "Name_ID", "Day", "Time", ema_items)

item_label <- function(x) {
  value <- attr(x, "label", exact = TRUE)
  if (is.null(value)) NA_character_ else as.character(value)
}
```

# Load the prepared analysis entry

The entry is loaded into a controlled environment and must contain only
`dat_focal_analysis`. Baseline rows are recovered by selecting the required
fields and keeping distinct rows; conflicting baseline responses within a
participant will fail the uniqueness checks below. EMA rows are not collapsed.
No raw data, private correction file or other Step 1 component RDA is needed.

```{r load-inputs}
input_environment <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
loaded_objects <- load(input_file, envir = input_environment)
if (!identical(loaded_objects, "dat_focal_analysis")) {
  stop("Input RDA must contain only dat_focal_analysis")
}
dat_focal_source <- input_environment$dat_focal_analysis

missing_baseline_variables <- setdiff(baseline_required, names(dat_focal_source))
missing_ema_variables <- setdiff(ema_required, names(dat_focal_source))

if (length(missing_baseline_variables)) {
  stop(
    "Baseline input is missing required variables: ",
    paste(missing_baseline_variables, collapse = ", ")
  )
}
if (length(missing_ema_variables)) {
  stop(
    "EMA input is missing required variables: ",
    paste(missing_ema_variables, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

dat_baseline_source <- dat_focal_source |>
  dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(baseline_required)) |>
  dplyr::distinct()
dat_ema_source <- dat_focal_source |>
  dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(ema_required))

input_overview <- data.frame(
  source = c("Baseline fields from prepared entry", "EMA fields from prepared entry"),
  object = c("dat_focal_analysis", "dat_focal_analysis"),
  rows = c(nrow(dat_baseline_source), nrow(dat_ema_source)),
  columns = c(ncol(dat_baseline_source), ncol(dat_ema_source)),
  participants = c(
    dplyr::n_distinct(dat_baseline_source$Name_ID),
    dplyr::n_distinct(dat_ema_source$Name_ID)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(input_overview)
```

# Validate source structure and coding

These checks implement the verified 209-participant, 30-day, three-prompt design
and fail before any output is written if the structural invariants are broken.

```{r validate-source-structure}
baseline_duplicate_ids <- dat_baseline_source |>
  dplyr::count(Name_ID, name = "n") |>
  dplyr::filter(n > 1L)

ema_duplicate_prompt_keys <- dat_ema_source |>
  dplyr::count(Name_ID, Day, Time, name = "n") |>
  dplyr::filter(n > 1L)

ema_duplicate_data_ids <- dat_ema_source |>
  dplyr::count(Data_ID, name = "n") |>
  dplyr::filter(n > 1L)

prompts_per_participant <- dat_ema_source |>
  dplyr::count(Name_ID, name = "scheduled_prompts")

days_per_participant <- dat_ema_source |>
  dplyr::distinct(Name_ID, Day) |>
  dplyr::count(Name_ID, name = "scheduled_days")

prompts_per_person_day <- dat_ema_source |>
  dplyr::count(Name_ID, Day, name = "scheduled_prompts")

baseline_ids <- sort(unique(dat_baseline_source$Name_ID))
ema_ids <- sort(unique(dat_ema_source$Name_ID))

all_baseline_items_numeric <- all(vapply(
  dat_baseline_source[baseline_all_items],
  is.numeric,
  logical(1)
))
all_ema_items_numeric <- all(vapply(
  dat_ema_source[ema_items],
  is.numeric,
  logical(1)
))

count_out_of_range <- function(data, items, valid_values) {
  sum(vapply(
    data[items],
    function(x) sum(!is.na(x) & !(x %in% valid_values)),
    integer(1)
  ))
}

baseline_out_of_range <-
  count_out_of_range(dat_baseline_source, baseline_items, 1:5) +
  count_out_of_range(dat_baseline_source, depression_items, 1:4) +
  count_out_of_range(dat_baseline_source, anxiety_items, 1:4) +
  count_out_of_range(dat_baseline_source, stress_items, 1:5)
ema_out_of_range <- sum(vapply(
  dat_ema_source[ema_items],
  function(x) sum(!is.na(x) & !(x %in% 1:5)),
  integer(1)
))

stopifnot(
  nrow(dat_baseline_source) == 209L,
  nrow(dat_ema_source) == 18810L,
  length(baseline_ids) == 209L,
  length(ema_ids) == 209L,
  identical(baseline_ids, ema_ids),
  nrow(baseline_duplicate_ids) == 0L,
  nrow(ema_duplicate_prompt_keys) == 0L,
  nrow(ema_duplicate_data_ids) == 0L,
  !anyNA(dat_baseline_source$Name_ID),
  !anyNA(dat_ema_source[c("Data_ID", "Name_ID", "Day", "Time")]),
  identical(sort(unique(dat_ema_source$Day)), 1:30),
  identical(sort(unique(dat_ema_source$Time)), 1:3),
  all(prompts_per_participant$scheduled_prompts == 90L),
  all(days_per_participant$scheduled_days == 30L),
  all(prompts_per_person_day$scheduled_prompts == 3L),
  all_baseline_items_numeric,
  all_ema_items_numeric,
  baseline_out_of_range == 0L,
  ema_out_of_range == 0L
)

structural_checks <- data.frame(
  check = c(
    "Baseline rows",
    "EMA scheduled rows",
    "Shared participants",
    "Duplicate baseline IDs",
    "Duplicate EMA prompt keys",
    "Duplicate EMA Data_ID values",
    "Days per participant",
    "Prompts per participant",
    "Prompts per person-day",
    "Baseline out-of-range item cells",
    "EMA out-of-range item cells"
  ),
  observed = c(
    nrow(dat_baseline_source),
    nrow(dat_ema_source),
    length(intersect(baseline_ids, ema_ids)),
    nrow(baseline_duplicate_ids),
    nrow(ema_duplicate_prompt_keys),
    nrow(ema_duplicate_data_ids),
    paste(range(days_per_participant$scheduled_days), collapse = "-"),
    paste(range(prompts_per_participant$scheduled_prompts), collapse = "-"),
    paste(range(prompts_per_person_day$scheduled_prompts), collapse = "-"),
    baseline_out_of_range,
    ema_out_of_range
  ),
  expected = c(
    "209",
    "18810",
    "209",
    "0",
    "0",
    "0",
    "30",
    "90",
    "3",
    "0",
    "0"
  ),
  passed = TRUE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(structural_checks)
```

# Extract the Step 2 item data

Baseline and EMA rows remain separate in a single list object. Sorting makes the
saved order deterministic without changing the prepared source RDA.

```{r extract-data}
dat_step2_baseline <- dat_baseline_source |>
  dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(baseline_required)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Name_ID) |>
  as.data.frame()

dat_step2_ema <- dat_ema_source |>
  dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(ema_required)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Name_ID, Day, Time) |>
  as.data.frame()

item_map <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(
    level = "Baseline",
    variable = baseline_items,
    item_number = 1:18,
    factor_group = ifelse(1:18 <= 6L, "Peripheral", "Core"),
    construct = "Trait PSMU",
    expected_min = 1,
    expected_max = 5,
    source_label = vapply(
      dat_step2_baseline[baseline_items],
      item_label,
      character(1)
    ),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ),
  data.frame(
    level = "Baseline",
    variable = depression_items,
    item_number = 1:7,
    factor_group = "Depression",
    construct = "Baseline depression",
    expected_min = 1,
    expected_max = 4,
    source_label = vapply(
      dat_step2_baseline[depression_items],
      item_label,
      character(1)
    ),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ),
  data.frame(
    level = "Baseline",
    variable = anxiety_items,
    item_number = 1:7,
    factor_group = "Anxiety",
    construct = "Baseline anxiety",
    expected_min = 1,
    expected_max = 4,
    source_label = vapply(
      dat_step2_baseline[anxiety_items],
      item_label,
      character(1)
    ),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ),
  data.frame(
    level = "Baseline",
    variable = stress_items,
    item_number = 1:10,
    factor_group = "Stress",
    construct = "Baseline perceived stress",
    expected_min = 1,
    expected_max = 5,
    source_label = vapply(
      dat_step2_baseline[stress_items],
      item_label,
      character(1)
    ),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ),
  data.frame(
    level = "EMA",
    variable = ema_items,
    item_number = 1:6,
    factor_group = ifelse(1:6 <= 2L, "Peripheral", "Core"),
    construct = "State PSMU manifestation",
    expected_min = 1,
    expected_max = 5,
    source_label = vapply(
      dat_step2_ema[ema_items],
      item_label,
      character(1)
    ),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(
    factor(level, levels = c("Baseline", "EMA")),
    factor(
      construct,
      levels = c(
        "Trait PSMU",
        "Baseline depression",
        "Baseline anxiety",
        "Baseline perceived stress",
        "State PSMU manifestation"
      )
    ),
    item_number
  ) |>
  as.data.frame()

knitr::kable(item_map)
```

# Build and save the canonical Step 2 object

The audit stores only compact provenance and structural facts. Temporary
descriptive summaries calculated later in this report are intentionally not
stored in the RDA.

```{r save-output}
source_files <- data.frame(
  role = "Prepared baseline and EMA source",
  file = "Res_2_Data_for_Analysis/dat_focal_analysis.rda",
  object = "dat_focal_analysis",
  md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(input_file)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

output_structure <- data.frame(
  component = c("baseline", "ema", "item_map"),
  observation_level = c("Participant", "Scheduled EMA prompt", "Item mapping"),
  rows = c(nrow(dat_step2_baseline), nrow(dat_step2_ema), nrow(item_map)),
  columns = c(ncol(dat_step2_baseline), ncol(dat_step2_ema), ncol(item_map)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

dat_step2_audit <- list(
  generated_by = "Step_2_Measurement_Models/S2_1_Prepare.Rmd",
  output_file = "Res_2_Data_for_Analysis/dat_step2_measurement.rda",
  source_files = source_files,
  structure = output_structure,
  checks = structural_checks
)

dat_step2_measurement <- list(
  baseline = dat_step2_baseline,
  ema = dat_step2_ema,
  item_map = item_map,
  audit = dat_step2_audit
)

stopifnot(
  identical(names(dat_step2_measurement), c("baseline", "ema", "item_map", "audit")),
  identical(names(dat_step2_measurement$baseline), baseline_required),
  identical(names(dat_step2_measurement$ema), ema_required),
  nrow(dat_step2_measurement$baseline) == 209L,
  nrow(dat_step2_measurement$ema) == 18810L,
  nrow(dat_step2_measurement$item_map) == 48L
)

save(dat_step2_measurement, file = output_file, compress = "xz", version = 3)

verification_environment <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
verified_objects <- load(output_file, envir = verification_environment)

if (!identical(verified_objects, "dat_step2_measurement")) {
  stop(
    "Output RDA must contain only dat_step2_measurement; found: ",
    paste(verified_objects, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

verified_step2 <- verification_environment$dat_step2_measurement

stopifnot(
  identical(verified_step2$baseline, dat_step2_baseline),
  identical(verified_step2$ema, dat_step2_ema),
  identical(verified_step2$item_map, item_map),
  identical(verified_step2$audit, dat_step2_audit)
)

output_manifest <- data.frame(
  file = "Res_2_Data_for_Analysis/dat_step2_measurement.rda",
  top_level_object = verified_objects,
  components = paste(names(verified_step2), collapse = ", "),
  bytes = file.info(output_file)$size,
  md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(output_file)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(output_structure)
knitr::kable(output_manifest)
```

# Descriptive checks of the saved Step 2 data

All tables and plots below use the object reloaded from the saved RDA. Numeric
summaries treat the 1--5 responses as numbers only to detect extraction or
coding anomalies. S2.2.1 uses ordinal WLSMV; S2.2.2 and the EMA multilevel
comparisons treat the indicators as continuous with MLR.

## Missingness and usable EMA prompts

```{r descriptive-missingness}
baseline_check <- verified_step2$baseline
ema_check <- verified_step2$ema

item_missingness <- function(data, items, level) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(items, function(item) {
    data.frame(
      level = level,
      item = item,
      n_total = nrow(data),
      n_observed = sum(!is.na(data[[item]])),
      n_missing = sum(is.na(data[[item]])),
      missing_percent = 100 * mean(is.na(data[[item]])),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }))
}

missingness_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  item_missingness(baseline_check, baseline_all_items, "Baseline"),
  item_missingness(ema_check, ema_items, "EMA")
)

ema_observed_item_count <- rowSums(!is.na(ema_check[ema_items]))

ema_prompt_patterns <- data.frame(
  pattern = c(
    "Complete on all 6 PMU items",
    "Partially complete on 1-5 PMU items",
    "Missing all 6 PMU items"
  ),
  prompts = c(
    sum(ema_observed_item_count == 6L),
    sum(ema_observed_item_count %in% 1:5),
    sum(ema_observed_item_count == 0L)
  ),
  percent = 100 * c(
    mean(ema_observed_item_count == 6L),
    mean(ema_observed_item_count %in% 1:5),
    mean(ema_observed_item_count == 0L)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

ema_check_with_complete <- ema_check |>
  dplyr::mutate(complete_pmu = ema_observed_item_count == 6L)

complete_by_time <- ema_check_with_complete |>
  dplyr::group_by(Time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    scheduled_prompts = dplyr::n(),
    complete_pmu_prompts = sum(complete_pmu),
    complete_percent = 100 * mean(complete_pmu),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

complete_by_participant <- ema_check_with_complete |>
  dplyr::group_by(Name_ID) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    scheduled_prompts = dplyr::n(),
    complete_pmu_prompts = sum(complete_pmu),
    complete_percent = 100 * mean(complete_pmu),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

participant_completeness_summary <- data.frame(
  statistic = c("Participants", "Mean", "SD", "Median", "Minimum", "Maximum"),
  complete_pmu_percent = c(
    nrow(complete_by_participant),
    mean(complete_by_participant$complete_percent),
    stats::sd(complete_by_participant$complete_percent),
    stats::median(complete_by_participant$complete_percent),
    min(complete_by_participant$complete_percent),
    max(complete_by_participant$complete_percent)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

stopifnot(
  all(missingness_table$n_missing[missingness_table$level == "Baseline"] == 0L),
  sum(ema_prompt_patterns$prompts) == nrow(ema_check),
  ema_prompt_patterns$prompts[ema_prompt_patterns$pattern == "Complete on all 6 PMU items"] > 0L,
  nrow(complete_by_participant) == 209L,
  all(complete_by_participant$complete_pmu_prompts > 0L)
)

knitr::kable(missingness_table, digits = 3)
knitr::kable(ema_prompt_patterns, digits = 3)
knitr::kable(complete_by_time, digits = 3)
knitr::kable(participant_completeness_summary, digits = 3)
```

## Item distributions

```{r descriptive-item-distributions}
item_descriptives <- function(data, items, level) {
  description <- psych::describe(data[items], fast = FALSE)
  data.frame(
    level = level,
    item = rownames(description),
    n_observed = description$n,
    mean = description$mean,
    sd = description$sd,
    median = description$median,
    minimum = description$min,
    maximum = description$max,
    skewness = description$skew,
    excess_kurtosis = description$kurtosis,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
    row.names = NULL
  )
}

baseline_descriptives <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  item_descriptives(baseline_check, baseline_items, "Baseline Trait PSMU"),
  item_descriptives(baseline_check, depression_items, "Baseline depression"),
  item_descriptives(baseline_check, anxiety_items, "Baseline anxiety"),
  item_descriptives(baseline_check, stress_items, "Baseline perceived stress")
)
ema_descriptives <- item_descriptives(
  ema_check,
  ema_items,
  "EMA"
)

descriptive_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  baseline_descriptives,
  ema_descriptives
)

descriptive_table <- descriptive_table |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    expected_maximum = dplyr::case_when(
      item %in% c(depression_items, anxiety_items) ~ 4,
      TRUE ~ 5
    )
  )

stopifnot(
  all(descriptive_table$minimum == 1),
  all(descriptive_table$maximum == descriptive_table$expected_maximum),
  all(is.finite(descriptive_table$mean)),
  all(descriptive_table$sd > 0)
)

knitr::kable(baseline_descriptives, digits = 3)
knitr::kable(ema_descriptives, digits = 3)
```

## Response-category coverage

```{r descriptive-category-coverage}
category_frequencies <- function(data, items, level, responses) {
  data |>
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(items)) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(
      cols = dplyr::everything(),
      names_to = "item",
      values_to = "response"
    ) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(response)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(response = as.integer(response)) |>
    dplyr::count(item, response, name = "n") |>
    tidyr::complete(
      item = items,
      response = responses,
      fill = list(n = 0L)
    ) |>
    dplyr::group_by(item) |>
    dplyr::mutate(percent_observed = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
    dplyr::ungroup() |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      level = level,
      item = factor(item, levels = items)
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(item, response)
}

baseline_category_frequency <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  category_frequencies(baseline_check, baseline_items, "Baseline Trait PSMU", 1:5),
  category_frequencies(baseline_check, depression_items, "Baseline depression", 1:4),
  category_frequencies(baseline_check, anxiety_items, "Baseline anxiety", 1:4),
  category_frequencies(baseline_check, stress_items, "Baseline perceived stress", 1:5)
)
ema_category_frequency <- category_frequencies(
  ema_check,
  ema_items,
  "EMA",
  1:5
)

category_coverage <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  baseline_category_frequency,
  ema_category_frequency
) |>
  dplyr::group_by(level, item) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    categories_observed = sum(n > 0L),
    smallest_category_n = min(n),
    largest_category_n = max(n),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

category_coverage <- category_coverage |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    expected_categories = dplyr::case_when(
      as.character(item) %in% c(depression_items, anxiety_items) ~ 4L,
      TRUE ~ 5L
    )
  )

stopifnot(all(category_coverage$categories_observed == category_coverage$expected_categories))

knitr::kable(category_coverage)
```

```{r category-distribution-plots, fig.width=11, fig.height=9}
ggplot2::ggplot(

) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(fill = "#4C78A8", width = 0.8) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ item, ncol = 6, scales = "free_y") +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Baseline Trait PSMU item response distributions",
    x = "Response category",
    y = "Percent of observed responses"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 10)

ggplot2::ggplot(
  ema_category_frequency,
  ggplot2::aes(x = factor(response), y = percent_observed)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(fill = "#F58518", width = 0.8) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ item, ncol = 3, scales = "free_y") +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "EMA PSMU item response distributions",
    x = "Response category",
    y = "Percent of observed responses"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```

## Scale-level and correlation checks

The following means and totals are calculated only inside this report to check
that the extracted items reproduce the expected scale distributions. They are
not written into `dat_step2_measurement.rda` and do not replace the planned CFA.

```{r descriptive-temporary-scale-checks}
stress_scored <- baseline_check[stress_items]
stress_reverse_items <- c("M_PSS_4", "M_PSS_5", "M_PSS_7", "M_PSS_8")
stress_scored[stress_reverse_items] <- lapply(
  stress_scored[stress_reverse_items],
  function(x) 6 - x
)

baseline_temporary <- data.frame(
  trait_psmu_total = rowSums(baseline_check[baseline_items]),
  trait_peripheral_mean = rowMeans(baseline_check[baseline_items[1:6]]),
  trait_core_mean = rowMeans(baseline_check[baseline_items[7:18]]),
  depression_total = rowSums(baseline_check[depression_items]),
  anxiety_total_0_3 = rowSums(
    as.data.frame(lapply(baseline_check[anxiety_items], function(x) x - 1))
  ),
  perceived_stress_total = rowSums(stress_scored)
)

ema_complete_rows <- stats::complete.cases(ema_check[ema_items])
ema_complete <- ema_check[ema_complete_rows, , drop = FALSE]
ema_temporary <- data.frame(
  state_psmu_mean = rowMeans(ema_complete[ema_items]),
  state_peripheral_mean = rowMeans(ema_complete[ema_items[1:2]]),
  state_core_mean = rowMeans(ema_complete[ema_items[3:6]])
)

temporary_summary <- function(data, level) {
  description <- psych::describe(data, fast = FALSE)
  data.frame(
    level = level,
    temporary_score = rownames(description),
    n = description$n,
    mean = description$mean,
    sd = description$sd,
    median = description$median,
    minimum = description$min,
    maximum = description$max,
    skewness = description$skew,
    excess_kurtosis = description$kurtosis,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
    row.names = NULL
  )
}

temporary_scale_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  temporary_summary(baseline_temporary, "Baseline"),
  temporary_summary(ema_temporary, "EMA complete prompts")
)

baseline_item_correlations <- stats::cor(
  baseline_check[baseline_all_items],
  use = "complete.obs"
)
ema_item_correlations <- stats::cor(
  ema_complete[ema_items],
  use = "complete.obs"
)

off_diagonal_summary <- function(correlation_matrix, level) {
  values <- correlation_matrix[lower.tri(correlation_matrix)]
  data.frame(
    level = level,
    item_pairs = length(values),
    minimum_correlation = min(values),
    mean_correlation = mean(values),
    maximum_correlation = max(values),
    perfect_absolute_correlations = sum(abs(values) >= 0.999999),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

correlation_sanity <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  off_diagonal_summary(baseline_item_correlations, "Baseline"),
  off_diagonal_summary(ema_item_correlations, "EMA complete prompts")
)

stopifnot(
  all(is.finite(as.matrix(baseline_item_correlations))),
  all(is.finite(as.matrix(ema_item_correlations))),
  all(correlation_sanity$perfect_absolute_correlations == 0L)
)

knitr::kable(temporary_scale_summary, digits = 3)
knitr::kable(correlation_sanity, digits = 3)
```

## EMA within- and between-person variation

As a final descriptive diagnostic, a random-intercept model is fitted separately
to each EMA item on the common six-item-complete prompt sample. The resulting
variance components and ICCs are data checks only; treating the ordinal item as
numeric here does not determine the estimator for the EMA CFA comparisons.

```{r descriptive-multilevel-variation}
ema_item_variation <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(ema_items, function(item) {
  model_formula <- stats::as.formula(paste0(item, " ~ 1 + (1 | Name_ID)"))
  fitted_model <- lme4::lmer(
    formula = model_formula,
    data = ema_complete,
    REML = TRUE,
    control = lme4::lmerControl(
      check.conv.singular = "ignore",
      optimizer = "bobyqa"
    )
  )

  variance_components <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(fitted_model))
  between_variance <- variance_components$vcov[variance_components$grp == "Name_ID"]
  within_variance <- variance_components$vcov[variance_components$grp == "Residual"]

  data.frame(
    item = item,
    prompts = stats::nobs(fitted_model),
    participants = dplyr::n_distinct(ema_complete$Name_ID),
    between_variance = between_variance,
    within_variance = within_variance,
    icc = between_variance / (between_variance + within_variance),
    singular = lme4::isSingular(fitted_model, tol = 1e-5),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))

stopifnot(
  all(ema_item_variation$prompts == sum(ema_complete_rows)),
  all(ema_item_variation$participants == 209L),
  all(ema_item_variation$between_variance > 0),
  all(ema_item_variation$within_variance > 0),
  all(ema_item_variation$icc > 0 & ema_item_variation$icc < 1),
  !any(ema_item_variation$singular)
)

knitr::kable(ema_item_variation, digits = 3)
```

```{r validation-checks, include=FALSE}
validation_checks <- data.frame(
  check = c(
    "Saved RDA contains one top-level object",
    "Saved object has baseline, ema, item_map, and audit components",
    "Baseline contains 209 unique participants and 42 complete raw items",
    "EMA preserves 18,810 scheduled prompts for 209 participants",
    "Baseline and EMA participant sets are identical",
    "All observed item responses follow their documented ranges",
    "Every item uses every documented response category",
    "No pair of extracted items is perfectly correlated",
    "Every EMA item has positive within- and between-person variance",
    "Temporary descriptive checks were not stored as output variables"
  ),
  passed = c(
    identical(verified_objects, "dat_step2_measurement"),
    identical(names(verified_step2), c("baseline", "ema", "item_map", "audit")),
    nrow(baseline_check) == 209L &&
      dplyr::n_distinct(baseline_check$Name_ID) == 209L &&
      !anyNA(baseline_check[baseline_all_items]),
    nrow(ema_check) == 18810L &&
      dplyr::n_distinct(ema_check$Name_ID) == 209L,
    identical(sort(unique(baseline_check$Name_ID)), sort(unique(ema_check$Name_ID))),
    baseline_out_of_range == 0L && ema_out_of_range == 0L,
    all(category_coverage$categories_observed == category_coverage$expected_categories),
    all(correlation_sanity$perfect_absolute_correlations == 0L),
    all(ema_item_variation$between_variance > 0) &&
      all(ema_item_variation$within_variance > 0),
    !any(c(
      "trait_psmu_total",
      "trait_peripheral_mean",
      "trait_core_mean",
      "depression_total",
      "anxiety_total_0_3",
      "perceived_stress_total"
    ) %in% names(verified_step2$baseline)) &&
      !any(c(
        "state_psmu_mean",
        "state_peripheral_mean",
        "state_core_mean"
      ) %in% names(verified_step2$ema))
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

if (!all(validation_checks$passed)) {
  stop(
    "Step 2 data validation failed: ",
    paste(validation_checks$check[!validation_checks$passed], collapse = "; ")
  )
}
```
